prompts.text: With the >31-hop routing ceiling lifted, re-attempt the gru_classifier assembly: place and route the full chain on ONE 10x12 chip, ship the full example collateral (.kyt/.grc/.py/golden/demo/README/tests), and gate it end to end on chip.

notes: EXAMPLE-CLASS row (wave 7). STILL BLOCKED, and the relay fix was NOT the missing piece. The example's offline collateral (feature front end, stimulus, goldens, 19 gates) was carried forward from the prior attempt unchanged and re-verified green in this tree; the whole-chain placement is what remains blocked. Independent re-measurement AFTER the hop ceiling was lifted: 2160 fresh layouts (18 legal GRU anchors x randomized small-block placements, deterministic auto_route_all) plus a second sweep across four routing MODELS (auto_orient, the single-backbone bus/ring v2 router, orient+bus, cpsat). The result reproduces the prior finding exactly -- the best layout is always exactly ONE net short, and the failing net's reason is 'no bus path from source to the broker tap', i.e. the RMS arm cannot reach a corridor. That is CORRIDOR CONGESTION, not hop count: no failing net on any attempted layout was a hop_overflow, so INV-36 (relay emission) is orthogonal to this wall and does not move it. Diagnosis for whoever picks this up: blocks total 65/120 cells but GRUCellBlock is 51 of them in a RIGID 7x8 fold, which partitions the free area into pockets; the join->GRU tail alone routes at 72/120. The lever is the GRU's fold (a narrower or reflowable footprint), or an RMS arm with fewer separately-placed blocks -- not the router's hop budget. The three known-limit guard tests in verification/tests/test_gru_classifier_example.py still hold and are deliberately left in place; they fail the day the geometry gives. No .kyt or .grc ships, because neither would run. HONEST NEGATIVE, TWICE MEASURED. The offline half is VERIFIED and landed (19 tests): RMS decomposition ComplexToMagSquared->MovingAverage(32,1/32)->Sqrt->KeepOneInN(32) within a DERIVED LEVEL-DEPENDENT truncation bound -(34*16384/y)-4 <= err <= +1 (0 violations over 1600 windows, tightest case 0.639 of bound — a FLAT tolerance would have been wrong by an order of magnitude between loud and quiet windows); ZCR bit-exact 0/480 against its pinned boundary-pair convention; all four stimulus segments voted correctly through the bit-exact GRU golden; four mutations proven to FAIL; three known-limit guards that fail the day the wall lifts. BLOCKED ON PLACEMENT, not correctness: ~2500 layouts in dispatch 1 and 5039 in dispatch 2 (2160 anchor sweep + 2879 across four routing models incl. auto_orient, single-backbone bus/ring, and CP-SAT) ALWAYS land exactly one net short with 'no bus path from source to the broker tap'. THE HOP CEILING WAS RULED OUT AS THE CAUSE: after INV-36 lifted it, NOT ONE hop_overflow appears in 5039 layouts. The wall is corridor CONGESTION: blocks total 65/120 cells but GRUCellBlock is 51 of them in a rigid 7x8 fold that partitions the free area into pockets the 4-block RMS arm cannot thread (the join->GRU tail alone routes at 72/120). THE LEVER IS THE GRU'S FOLD OR A SHORTER RMS ARM, NOT THE ROUTER. MODEL-SIDE FINDING (independent of placement): the Q15 power stage and the trained model's own distribution are in tension — gain_range sets a clip's RMS while saturation is driven by its PEAK, and crest factors vary by class (4-FSK 1.27 ... SSB 3.59 median), so peak|z|>1 for 100% of SSB and 79% of noise training clips; invisible to the float reference, clips a fixed-point front end hard (error to -1247 LSB), and peak-normalising is NOT a free fix (it made the OFFLINE reference vote wrong).
